Axiom:
This role's bash commands stay within this list: - **Must run:** exact `sdd-verify --task --phase ` exactly once per attempt at the phase protocol's STEP_5. That step owns repair order, target derivation and foundation semantics; this axiom only permits the invocation. Never wrap it in whole-project `npm run fix`, and never run the audit-owned `sdd-verify --profile full` from a phase. Its receipt is the result; do not copy it into prose log lines. - **May run:** `ls ` for targeted recon (NOT `-la` or recursive); `tsc --noEmit` after code changes; `node --test ` for test-kind phases; `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` for timestamps. - **May run:** `sdd-extract ` — extract anchored section from ticket/spec. - **May run:** exact `unlink ` and `rmdir ` while implementing the phase; no glob, recursion, or undeclared deletion. A failed verification has no receipt, so a retry after the fix is a new attempt and invokes the canonical command once again. - **May run:** `gennady lint --spec= ` only for a genuinely additional explicit check outside phase verification. STEP_5 already passes the owning spec and exact phase targets internally; do not duplicate it there. - **Bootstrap-only dependency addition:** ONLY when phase kind is `bootstrap`, its Objective names adding that dependency, and Target Files contain `package.json` plus the active npm lock file, may run exactly `npm view engines`, `npm view version`, and `npm view dist-tags`, then one-package `npm install --save-dev --save-exact @` or `npm add --save-dev --save-exact @` for a dev tool; for a runtime dependency, one-package `npm install @` or `npm add @`. No other npm/network command, option, tag, unversioned package, or multi-package install is permitted. Non-bootstrap phases have no dependency-addition exemption.
Trust the context handed at dispatch — ticket, spec, manifest, diff — as current: it MUST be used as-is, not re-derived through bash. When a step in this directive names a real gap beyond what was handed (new commits since dispatch, a sibling branch, a file's history), `git`/`gh` reads (`status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `blame`, `gh pr view`/`diff`) are the legal way to close it. Mutating the repository (`git add`/`commit`/`push`/`rebase`/`reset`, `gh pr create`/`merge`) stays reserved for the step that owns publish/commit.
Absent such a step, treat `git`/`gh` as off the table: re-deriving handed context costs ~100-300ms per call for zero value, and full project recon / repository mutation belong to the orchestrator or authoring flow, not this role.
All recon stays inside the project root. A fact that genuinely lives outside it — a global `~/.npmrc`, a system-wide setting, anything outside this checkout — is not a gap this role closes by reading it anyway, read-only or not: no bash command in this list reaches outside the project root, and none should be improvised to. That fact is `H_BLOCKED` per `AX_BLOCKER_ESCALATION` with the specific question named — the operator is the channel for what the sandbox cannot see, not a last resort after trying anyway.
**Temp files stay under `.claude/tmp/`, nowhere else.** Any scratch or trial file this role needs — a throwaway script, an intermediate probe output — is created ONLY under `.claude/tmp/` inside the project root: create the directory when it does not yet exist, and remove what was created once it stops being needed (shared, reused across roles and other purposes — not this phase's private space to leave dirty). The system `/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`, and the repository root are closed for this: a root-level scratch file pollutes the diff and gets caught by the same inventory/lint gates meant for real `Target Files`, and `/tmp`/`$TMPDIR` sit outside the checkout this role's recon is scoped to above.
**Forbidden:** any npm/network command outside the exact bootstrap-only forms above; `npm run fix`; `npm run check`; `npm run lint` alone (overkill — use `sdd-verify` or `tsc --noEmit` for narrower checks); `npm run format`; `prettier` directly — repair and verification both live INSIDE `sdd-verify`, never called piecemeal; any recursive or project-wide file scan; any command that reads unrelated files for «context».
Ticket §5 commands are not a phase-agent exemption: the one `sdd-verify --task ... --phase ...` invocation runs applicable rows itself and owns their receipt (`AX_VERIFICATION_BEFORE_HANDOFF`). `sdd-verify` remains the sole self-initiated mutator through its exact-target repair rung; a standalone §5, format, lint or fix invocation remains forbidden.
